title: esbuild
description: Use esbuild as a bundler, minifier, and transform API — and understand what its speed costs in flexibility.

data.text: esbuild is written in Go and parallelises parsing, linking, and code generation across CPU cores. It is often 10–100× faster than JavaScript-based tooling, which is why Vite, tsup, and many CLIs use it internally.

data.title: Bundle and minify in one command
data.code:
npm install -D esbuild
npx esbuild src/index.ts --bundle --minify --sourcemap --target=es2020 --outfile=dist/bundle.js
npx esbuild src/index.ts --bundle --format=esm --splitting --outdir=dist

data.caption: scripts/build.ts — programmatic build with metafile analysis

data.text: `external` keeps peer dependencies out of the bundle, `loader` tells esbuild how to treat non-JS imports, and `metafile` produces a JSON description of the output that you can feed into bundle-analysis tools.

data.title: Speed trades away flexibility
data.text: esbuild does not run TypeScript type checking, has a smaller plugin API than Webpack/Rollup, and cannot express every custom transform. Use it for speed, and keep `tsc --noEmit` in CI.

terms.definition: Resolve the import graph and emit one or more output files.
JSON describing inputs, outputs, and byte sizes, used for bundle analysis.
Emitting shared chunks for dynamic imports when format is esm.
The JavaScript language level esbuild should emit (for example es2020).

data.title: Key takeaways
points: esbuild is a Go bundler/transform tool known for speed.
It powers Vite dev transforms and many library build tools.
It does not type-check; pair it with tsc --noEmit.
Use external for peer dependencies and metafile for analysis.
data.takeaway: Interviewers like the trade-off: esbuild buys speed by doing less than Webpack.
